score_meanings.promise_vocabulary: 0 drifts into claims/profiles/central trust-ledger framing, 5 stays promise-first and pCID-specific
score_meanings.simplicity_durability: 0 overbuilt or fragile, 5 minimal, durable, and small-device-friendly under the 100-year goal

assessment.rationale: Poor fit for live CRDT pressure. It can carry durable audit publications, but making subject/assertion/proof universal adds global parser burden, weakens unknown-pCID and mixed-version behavior, and does not supply a credible reliable live binding. As a negative control it is useful mainly for showing why richer audit structure should stay payload-local, not universal.
strengths: Deterministic CBOR array is straightforward to parse and implement.
Built-in assertion/proof slots can help later human or LLM audit of published snapshots.
weaknesses: Universal outer-envelope structure is a bad match for sub-second live CRDT transport pressure.
Removing a minimal universal [pcid,payload] dispatch slot hurts evolution and unknown-protocol handling.
Subject/assertion/proof framing is not promise-first vocabulary and pushes Gordian semantics onto every payload.
risks: Higher small-device and 100-year parser burden across all traffic.
Audit-layer structure may leak into live-channel design and blur layer claims.
Partitions, reordering, and delayed publication are not handled beyond generic envelope shape.
open_questions: Should live state stay off-grid until a reliable ordered binding exists?
What exact content-addressed snapshot object would the audit publication cite?
Can the audit/proof structure be kept inside a payload family instead of the universal envelope?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.
